summary_paragraph: A woman with long-standing type 1 diabetes, diabetic neuropathy, retinopathy, nephropathy, gastroparesis, and a history of foot ulcers was admitted for surgical management of a right foot ulcer. She underwent a right foot exostectomy with excision and closure of the ulcer. Postoperatively, she received IV antibiotics and was transitioned back to oral antibiotics. Her pain was managed with tramadol and oxycodone-acetaminophen as needed, and her blood glucose was controlled with insulin. Labs remained stable, with no signs of infection or kidney dysfunction. She was discharged home with visiting nurse services, strict non-weight-bearing instructions for the right foot, and follow-up planned with her podiatrist. Her medications were adjusted, including discontinuation of losartan and addition of furosemide for potential swelling.
